workflow_definition.description: Baseline 7-agent sequential IT incident triage and remediation workflow.

optimization_opportunities: Dynamic routing for simple vs complex incidents
Bypassing symptom diagnostic branch for low-complexity / known-issue incidents
Parallel execution of runbook retrieval and symptom correlation
Early stopping when runbook confidence exceeds 0.95 and severity is SEV-4
optimizer_annotations.hypothesis_disclaimer: Declared candidate hypothesis from workflow specification, not an empirical or validated optimization opportunity.

agents.goal: Categorize the incident into a precise failure domain (network_failure, application_error, authentication_issue, database_problem, storage_exhaustion) and assess complexity level (Simple, Moderate, Complex) for dynamic routing.
agents.backstory: You are a Senior Systems Architect who excels at recognizing system failure topologies, root failure domains, and whether an incident is standard or multi-service complex.

tasks.description: f'Based on the intake findings below, classify the primary failure category (network_failure, application_error, authentication_issue, database_problem, storage_exhaustion) and apparent complexity (Simple, Moderate, Complex):\nIntake Findings: {intake_text}'
tasks.expected_output: JSON containing category, apparent_complexity, and classification_reasoning.

prompts: f'Based on the intake findings below, classify the primary failure category (network_failure, application_error, authentication_issue, database_problem, storage_exhaustion) and apparent complexity (Simple, Moderate, Complex):\nIntake Findings: {intake_text}'
Backstory: You are a Senior Systems Architect who excels at recognizing system failure topologies, root failure domains, and whether an incident is standard or multi-service complex.

agents.goal: Normalize raw incident ticket text, extract affected services, symptoms, timestamps, and impacted users, and flag any missing critical fields without inventing facts.
agents.backstory: You are a Tier-1 SRE Intake Specialist. You parse messy, emergency incident tickets into crisp, unambiguous facts and telemetry without speculating or adding unsupported assumptions.

tasks.description: f'Normalize this raw incident ticket and extract structured fields:\nRaw Ticket: {json.dumps(incident_input, indent=2)}\nReturn JSON with: normalized_title, affected_service, symptoms, timestamps, reported_impact_users, outage_minutes, and missing_fields.'
tasks.expected_output: Valid JSON string containing normalized incident telemetry and missing fields.

prompts: f'Normalize this raw incident ticket and extract structured fields:\nRaw Ticket: {json.dumps(incident_input, indent=2)}\nReturn JSON with: normalized_title, affected_service, symptoms, timestamps, reported_impact_users, outage_minutes, and missing_fields.'
Backstory: You are a Tier-1 SRE Intake Specialist. You parse messy, emergency incident tickets into crisp, unambiguous facts and telemetry without speculating or adding unsupported assumptions.

agents.goal: Recommend structured, reversible, and safe troubleshooting actions based on retrieved runbooks and incident evidence. Never execute commands or connect to real infrastructure.
agents.backstory: You are a Senior Infrastructure Automation Engineer focused on safe system recovery. You specify explicit rollback procedures and safety prerequisites for every action.

tasks.expected_output: JSON with ordered remediation_steps, rollback_plan, and safety_verification.

prompts: Backstory: You are a Senior Infrastructure Automation Engineer focused on safe system recovery. You specify explicit rollback procedures and safety prerequisites for every action.

agents.goal: Audit findings across intake, classification, runbooks, symptoms, severity, and remediation. Detect contradictions or unsupported claims and compile the final structured JSON incident triage report.
agents.backstory: You are the Principal SRE Review Lead. You ensure incident reports maintain the highest standards of factual consistency, SLA compliance, and remediation safety.

tasks.expected_output: Complete final incident triage JSON report.

prompts: Backstory: You are the Principal SRE Review Lead. You ensure incident reports maintain the highest standards of factual consistency, SLA compliance, and remediation safety.

agents.goal: Examine candidate runbooks from the local knowledge base, evaluate symptom matches, and select the optimal runbook IDs with supporting evidence.
agents.backstory: You are an Operations Reliability Engineer who knows every standard operating procedure and selects the most relevant, proven runbook for active incidents.

tasks.expected_output: JSON with selected_runbook_id, match_confidence, prerequisites, and safety_notes.

prompts: Backstory: You are an Operations Reliability Engineer who knows every standard operating procedure and selects the most relevant, proven runbook for active incidents.

agents.goal: Apply deterministic corporate severity thresholds and evaluate contextual impact, returning the final severity level (SEV-1 to SEV-4) and complete justification.
agents.backstory: You are an Incident Commander responsible for assigning definitive incident severity levels, strictly adhering to SLA policies and business continuity guidelines.

tasks.expected_output: JSON with severity_level, governing_sla_rule, and justification.

prompts: Backstory: You are an Incident Commander responsible for assigning definitive incident severity levels, strictly adhering to SLA policies and business continuity guidelines.

agents.goal: Correlate active incident symptoms with synthetic historical incidents and log records. Identify recurring patterns and return matching historical IDs and evidence.
agents.backstory: You are a Root Cause Diagnostics Specialist who performs deep telemetry correlation across past outages to spot systemic regressions and recurring anomalies.

tasks.expected_output: JSON with correlated_incident_ids, recurring_patterns, and diagnostic_stage_assessment.

prompts: Backstory: You are a Root Cause Diagnostics Specialist who performs deep telemetry correlation across past outages to spot systemic regressions and recurring anomalies.

sample_outputs.normalized_title: inventory-api: Thread deadlock detected in OrderFulfillmentWorker (inventory-api)

sample_outputs.classification_reasoning: The intake reports a thread deadlock in the OrderFulfillmentWorker of the inventory‑api service. A deadlock is an internal application logic/concurrency issue rather than a network, authentication, database, or storage problem, matching the ground‑truth category of application_error. Resolving a deadlock typically requires code analysis, lock ordering review, and possibly changes to threading models, which involves multiple components within the service but does not usually require a full system redesign. This places the incident at a moderate level of operational complexity.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
Kubectl context set to production cluster
sample_outputs.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

recurring_patterns.symptom_pattern: inventory-api: Thread deadlock detected in OrderFulfillmentWorker

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Historical correlation indicates recurring pattern in inventory-api.

sample_outputs.governing_sla_rule: Tier-1 service impacting >= 500 users, or cross-tier impact >= 2,000 users.
sample_outputs.justification: The incident impacts 3,500 users, exceeding the 2,000‑user cross‑tier threshold defined in the SLA rule. Although the affected service is Tier‑2, the user count alone triggers the SEV‑2 classification. The outage duration of 55 minutes is within the response window for SEV‑2 (typically < 1 hour for initial acknowledgment and remediation), and the root cause has been confirmed with high confidence (0.95). Therefore, the deterministic rule and the contextual metrics both validate a final severity level of SEV‑2.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Cluster Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the operator has the required root or ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster.
verification: AWS identity ARN matches ProdOperations role
kubectl context name contains 'prod'
Node list shows expected production node names

remediation_steps.title: Verify Write‑Freeze and Promote Read‑Replica
remediation_steps.description: Confirm that no write traffic is in flight, then promote the standby read‑replica to become the primary database for inventory‑api.
verification: Write‑freeze metric returns 0
Primary DB instance status changes to 'available' and role = 'writer'
Read‑replica status changes to 'promoted'

remediation_steps.title: Graceful Rolling Restart of inventory‑api Pods
remediation_steps.description: Perform a rolling restart to clear the deadlocked OrderFulfillmentWorker threads while preserving service continuity.
verification: All pods reach READY 1/1 and STATUS Running within 5 minutes
kubectl logs -l app=inventory-api --tail=20 | grep -i 'deadlock' returns no matches

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Validate that the service health endpoint is healthy and that error rates have dropped to baseline.
verification: Health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body 'OK'
Error metric count is 0 or below threshold (<5 per minute)
CPU/Memory usage within normal range (<70% of request limits)

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert the deployment to the previous container image tag and, if needed, demote the promoted replica back to read‑only while re‑establishing the original primary.

steps.description: Undo the rolling restart by rolling back to the prior image tag.
verification: Pods restart with the previous image tag (verify via kubectl describe pod)
Previous deadlock state does not reappear within 10 minutes

steps.description: If the promoted replica caused data divergence, demote it and re‑attach the original primary.
verification: Primary endpoint points back to original instance
Replication lag returns to <5 seconds

steps.description: Re‑run health audit to confirm service stability after rollback.
verification: Health endpoint returns HTTP 200
Error metric remains at baseline

prerequisite_checks: Rollback procedure documented and approved by change management
Current deployment image tag recorded for undo
